sam: Heads up 1: MercuryBank POC says no peering allowed. They insist on PrivateLink + their TGW -> onprem. NetOps wants a concrete allowlist + steps. Can SEs confirm pattern?

neha: PrivateLink works. Key things to call out: endpoint ENIs appear in customer subnets, Private DNS option determines whether our FQDN resolves to the endpoint. It's not TGWtransitive by default; TGW can reach interface endpoints if the interface lives in a VPC that the TGW attaches to and routes are configured.

diego: TL;DR checklist I use for banks: 1) Customer creates interface endpoint(s) in at least two AZs in a subnet that TGW can reach. 2) They share endpoint IDs. 3) We accept the service connection. 4) Customer enables private DNS (or we give them alternate internal FQDN). 5) SGs: allow outbound to endpoint SG / ENI IPs on TCP 443.

customer-netops: Can you provide exact sample SG rules and whether we need NAT for the POC?

neha: Sample SG (drop into their firewall ticket):
```
# Sample security group / firewall snippet
# From: app subnets or TGW attachment VPC
# To: Interface endpoint ENI(s)
- Allow TCP 443 from 10.10.0.0/16 (app CIDR) -> <endpoint-ENI-IP-1>,<endpoint-ENI-IP-2>
- Allow TCP 8443 (optional) from ops CIDR -> <endpoint-ENI-IP-1>
# If they can't reference ENI SG, allow by endpoint FQDN via proxy or allowlist the Egress NLB range we provide in contract.
```

diego: NAT: Not required if all egress is to internal endpoints (PrivateLink, S3 interface endpoints). However, initial image/model downloads often pull from public S3 or external host. Options: a) stage artifacts in customer's S3 and grant us a read role, b) allow temporary NAT egress for bootstrap, or c) use a proxy in their VPC that we can call via PrivateLink. 

sam: They asked for static IP ranges to put into their corporate perimeter firewall. We can't promise global static IPs for hosted infra, but for a POC we can provide perAZ ENI CIDRs that are likely stable for ~30 days. Otherwise recommend allowlist by SG + DNS/SNI or use mTLS.

customer-netops: If we enable private DNS, will the DNS name be identical to public API hostname? We need to audit our DNS records.

neha: Yes, if private DNS is enabled the AWS endpoint will return the service's canonical name internally (same FQDN). If they prefer separate names, we can publish an internal-only CNAME to the endpoint DNS. Call out: they must not block AWS VPC DNS (169.254.169.253/UDP or the .2 resolver) for private resolution.

diego: Operational checklist to send in the meeting:
1) Confirm subnets & AZs where endpoints will be created.
2) Customer creates interface endpoint(s) for our service and shares IDs.
3) We accept connection and confirm endpoint SG group.
4) Customer updates route tables/TGW route propagation so bastions/TGW-attached VPCs can reach endpoint ENIs.
5) Enable VPC Flow Logs for troubleshooting.
6) Test: curl -v https://<svc-fqdn> from bastion (show sample curl).

sam: Quick cost note for sales: interface endpoints incur hourly + data processing charges on AWS side; customer will see endpoint+data charges on their AWS bill. Our usage billing remains normal. Add this to the SOW as "customer endpoint charges may apply."

customer-netops: Will TLS client certs help avoid IP churn issues?
neha: Absolutely. mTLS or client cert verification + SNI allowlist reduces need to change firewall rules on ENI IP churn. For POC we usually accept SG allowlist and ask for a 2-week window for any IP changes.

diego: Also call out the nontransitive caveat again: if their onprem goes through TGW -> Transit VPC -> attachments, verify the endpoint's ENIs are in a VPC that TGW routes to, or put a small proxy in the TGW attachment VPC.

sam: I'll send this condensed checklist and a sample SG template. Booking 45m with MercuryBank NetOps for Friday 9am ET. @customer-netops please confirm what subnets you plan to use and whether you'll enable private DNS. :calendar:

deploy-bot: doc-created: sales/handbooks/mercury-privatelink-onboarding-draft (for review).

customer-netops: Confirmed 1. We'll share subnets and TGW diagram before Friday. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

neha: One last item: remind them to open access to the endpoint ENI IPs in their IDS/IPS so health checks and flow logs are not flagged as blocked traffic during validation.

sam: Great. I'll attach the SG snippet + cost note to the invite and loop in legal for the SOW line about endpoint charges.
